answer_text: Official docs: Confluent consumer configuration reference https://docs.confluent.io/platform/current/installation/configuration/consumer-configs.html [r4]. max.poll.records = maximum records returned in a single poll() (default 500); it does not change fetching, records are cached and returned incrementally [r4]. fetch.min.bytes = minimum bytes the broker responds with (default 1); the broker waits up to fetch.wait.max.ms to accumulate it [r5]. Direction (Confluent doc): increase max.poll.records to batch more records, increase fetch.min.bytes to wait for more data per batch, and raise max.poll.interval.ms if processing is slow [r3].
notes: Both settings + official URL; latency trade-off of fetch.min.bytes not stated.

answer_text: Official Apache Kafka consumer configs (4.3) https://kafka.apache.org/43/configuration/consumer-configs/ [r1]: fetch.min.bytes = minimum amount of data the server returns for a fetch request; with the default 1 byte, fetches are answered as soon as any data is available [r1][r2]. max.poll.records is not in the returned excerpts, and no tuning direction is given.
